Explore how I would support a growing business across a working week. Each sample is a simulated assignment, with a concrete deliverable, a proposed success measure and a downloadable working table. No client results are implied.

MY APPROACH / THE EXECUTIVE OPERATING RHYTHM

Before the meeting. After the decision. Until the work is done.

01 / Anticipate

Review the week ahead, identify conflicts, prepare briefs and protect focus time.

02 / Prioritise

Separate urgent issues from routine requests. Present options and escalate decisions beyond my authority.

03 / Coordinate

Confirm owners, deadlines, dependencies and stakeholder expectations.

04 / Close the loop

Track commitments, surface exceptions and confirm completion with evidence.

RESEARCH & ANALYSIS / SOURCE-BASED BRIEF

What executive offices expect beyond administration

Question: Where can an executive assistant create the most operational value?

Findings: Three published role descriptions emphasise protecting strategic time, preparing decision-ready materials and tracking commitments across teams. The practical implication is to organise support around priorities and exceptions, not simply completed tasks.

Recommendation: Agree a weekly priority review, a meeting preparation checklist and one shared action register. Establish a baseline before setting improvement targets.

Limitations: This is a qualitative review of three role descriptions, not a representative labour-market survey.

Sources: Orbis — executive office role · Tenece — group executive assistant · British Chambers of Commerce — role pack. Reviewed November 2026.

Client project · Sole designer and builder

Safiyah’s Gleam

A digital wedding invitation guests can use to RSVP, get directions, and give a gift. One link also gives the couple a way to organize responses and follow up after the wedding.

Everything guests need in one link

I mapped the full experience, then designed and built the website for my client’s wedding. Guests could find the couple’s photos, wedding date, schedule, venue, and dress code without searching through separate messages. A Google Maps link opens directions to the venue.

I also designed what happens after a guest responds or gives a gift, so the couple can see who replied and who to thank.

From invitation to thank-you

Switch views to see what guests can do and what the couple can see.

Guest experience

  1. Open the inviteSee the couple’s photos, wedding date, schedule, and dress code.
  2. Get directionsTap the location to open the venue in Google Maps.
  3. RSVP onlineConfirm attendance electronically through the invitation.
  4. Give a giftBrowse the couple’s wishlist or use the bank details they provide for a direct transfer.

Host workflow

  1. Share one linkSend the invitation with photos and event details in one place.
  2. Make arrival easierPoint guests to the venue from the invitation with Google Maps.
  3. See who repliedGet visibility into RSVPs through WhatsApp or a private dashboard.
  4. Track gifts and say thanksSet up a gift list, add transfer details, and use the private gift dashboard to see who gave and thank them after the wedding.

About me

I believe good executive support goes beyond keeping things organised.

I am naturally curious about how businesses operate, how decisions are executed and what prevents teams from working efficiently.

See more

My professional experience in healthcare taught me the importance of accuracy, discretion, clear communication and timely follow-through. It also shaped how I approach responsibilities in environments where overlooked details can have significant consequences.

My interest in executive support and business operations comes from a desire to make work easier for leaders and their teams.

I enjoy bringing structure to competing priorities, researching information, coordinating responsibilities, anticipating needs and finding practical ways to improve how work gets done.

I combine administrative capabilities with systems thinking, commercial awareness and modern productivity tools to support effective decision-making and business execution.

Ultimately, I want my contribution to be reflected in how smoothly the business operates, how effectively the team executes and how much time leadership can dedicate to moving the organisation forward.
